item.title: Overview
item.description: LeMat-Synth is an open-source multi-modal toolbox for extracting structured synthesis procedures and performance data from materials science literature at scale. It was presented at NeurIPS AI4Mat 2025.

item.title: Dataset Access
item.description: LeMat-Synth publishes two datasets on the HuggingFace Hub. Both are gated — access is granted automatically, but you must request it once and be authenticated.

item.title: Tutorials
item.description: Seven runnable notebooks that take you from reading LeMat-Synth data to producing it, and finally to changing what gets produced. Each one is self-contained, states its prerequisites and cost up front, and explains what every step is doing rather than just executing it.

item.title: Thermocatalysis
item.description: End-to-end workflow for ammonia-decomposition catalysts: extract synthesis procedures and conversion-vs-temperature curves from a folder of PDFs, then score several vision models against human-annotated ground truth.

item.title: Superconductors
item.description: Extracts synthesis procedures and critical temperatures (Tc) from superconductor papers. Tc is read twice — once from the text, and once geometrically from ρ(T) or R(T) plots — which gives a built-in cross-check on both readings.

item.title: Porous Materials
item.description:
Extracts synthesis procedures and adsorption isotherms from papers on MOFs, zeolites, COFs and related frameworks.

This is the simplest of the three case studies — no domain metric extractors, no custom writer — which makes it the best template to copy when starting a new domain. Building your own case study walks through exactly how it is assembled.

item.title: Build Your Own
item.description: Pointing LeMat-Synth at a new scientific domain — electrochemistry, battery cycling, thermoelectrics, photocatalysis — does not require touching the pipeline. You assemble a DomainConfig from four pieces and hand it to BatchRunner, which already knows how to find PDFs, detect supplementary files, retry on rate limits, resume interrupted runs, and report progress.

item.title: CLI Reference
item.description:
The lemat-synth command-line tool lets you extract structured synthesis procedures from materials science papers without writing any Python code.

Both commands accept the same key=value overrides, which can be used to change models, prompts, output paths, and other settings. See Quick Reference: All Arguments below.
